end_ms.description: The time in milliseconds since the start of the video when the shot ended.

errors.description: Grouping for detected errors resulting from this shot. Omitted if there are no discernible errors.

dead_dink.description: Set as `exploited` if we detect a definite dead dink that was exploited, otherwise omitted (we do not currently detect potential dead dinks). To be considered a dead dink, the shot_type must be a dink or drop and the opponent's return shot must be a groundstroke that is hit above the net height. Status: not supported, not planned

faults.description: A fault is a type of error that violates the rules of the game, thus ending the rally. This includes both actual and potential faults (that were saved by the opponent, or somehow overlooked and didn't end the rally). Omitted if none were detected. If this field is present but `is_final` is false, it means play continued despite the fault (i.e., either players overlooked a fault or the AI detected a potential fault that was not called).

excess_bounce.description: `true` if the ball bounced more than once before being hit, `false` if the ball only bounced once, omitted if unknown.

kitchen.description: `true` if player stepped in the kitchen while volleying, `false` if they did not, omitted if unknown.

net.description: `true` if the ball was stopped by the net, `false` if the ball did clear the net (even if it touched).

out.description: Information about the ball potentially or actually going out.

direction.description: The direction the ball was (potentially or actually) going out.

outcome.description: Whether the shot actually landed out, or was intercepted (erroneously) by an opponent.

side.description: The side of the court the ball was (potentially or actually) going out if the direction is lateral (left or right). Omitted if not going out laterally.

paddle_hit_net.description: `true` if paddle hit the net, `false` if the paddle did not hit the net, omitted if unknown.

short.description: `true` if the ball is hit by the player to land on the same court side, before the net, but not out. `false` if the ball didn't land on the same court side, omitted if unknown.

popup.description:
Set if we detect a definite or potential popup, which is currently
defined as: either the shot popping up more than 3.5 feet from the strike point,
or crossing the net at 2.2 feet above while popping up at least 2.6 feet from
the strike point.

`exploited` if it was exploited by the opponent team. `potential` if it was a popup that was not exploited. (Determined by whether it was volleyed)

is_final.description: Whether this is the final shot in the rally.

is_passing.description: Whether this shot passed the *nearest* opponent without them touching it. Omitted if unknown.

is_poach.description:
Whether this ball was hit closer to the non-hitter's position than the hitter's position along the width of the court, and in front of the non-hitter.

The players' positions are measured at the time the previous shot was hit,
and the ball's position is determined at the time the ball was hit by the receiving team.

A poach is only possible if the ball is hit in front of the player the ball was poached from (their teammate).

If the ball goes past the non-hitter and their partner hits it, it is not considered a poach,
regardless of the x-axis differential between the players and the ball.

Omitted if unknown.

is_reset.description: Whether this shot takes significant pace off the ball. Omitted if unknown or not applicable.

is_speedup.description:
To be considered a speedup, the following conditions must be met:

- the shot adds significant pace on the ball
- the hitting player is near the kitchen
- at least one of the opposing players is near the kitchen

Omitted if unknown or not applicable.

is_volley.description: Whether this shot was a volley hit out of the air or not. Omitted if unknown.

player_id.description: The ID of the player who hit the ball.
player_id.title: Player ID

quality.description: an evaluation of the quality of the shot

execution.description: how well the shot was executed
execution.title: Quality Score

overall.description: the combination of the execution and selection qualities
overall.title: Quality Score

selection.description: how good of a choice it was to hit this shot
selection.title: Quality Score

resulting_ball_movement.description: Stats related to how the ball moves as a result of being hit. Omitted if we couldn't track the ball after the shot was made.

direction.description: Direction that the ball was hit from and to.

pitch.description:
The pitch angle, in degrees within a range of [-90, 90].

- 0 degrees: straight shot (parallel to the ground)
- 90 degrees: shot directly upwards (perpendicular to the ground)
- -90 degrees: shot directly downwards (perpendicular to the ground)
pitch.title: Pitch Angle

yaw.description:
The yaw angle, in degrees within a range of (-180, 180].

- 0 degrees: shot towards the left sideline (parallel to player's own baseline)
- 90 degrees: shot towards the net directly (perpendicular to player's own baseline)
- 180 degrees: shot towards the right sideline (parallel to player's own baseline)
- Negative values are the same, but in the opposite direction (backwards).
yaw.title: Yaw Angle

crossed_net.description: `true` if the ball crosses the net plane, else `false`. Note that this value will be `true` for ATPs (they cross the net plane without the ball necessarily ever going higher than the net).

distance.description: The distance the ball traveled (feet) before coming in contact with the net, court, paddle, etc.

distance_from_baseline.description: The distance the ball landed from the opponent's baseline.

height_over_net.description:
The height the ball in feet when it _reaches_ the plane of the net. This is
omitted if the ball never reaches the net plane. A ball that reaches the net but
does not go over will have this value set to the height of the ball when it
reaches the net (usually this will be greater than 0 but lower than the net
height). Similarly, a ball that grazes the net cord and topples over will have
its height over the net as roughly the height of the net at that location.

Note that the plane of the net exists at `y = 22`.

is_volleyed.description: Whether the ball was hit out of the air or not.

speed.description: Speed of the ball in MPH.

spin.description: The spin of the ball after it was hit. Omitted if unknown.

dominant_class.description: The dominant spin class of the ball.

magnitude.description: The magnitude of the spin in RPM.

trajectory.description:
Describes the estimated flight path of a ball after it was hit by the player.

The ball essentially flies in a 2D projectile motion along a 2D plane. One dimension
of this plane is aligned with the Z-axis. An estimation of its path through 3D space
can be reconstructed from its initial flight characteristics and start and end
points.

confidence.description: Our confidence in this trajectory (based on our confidence in the start and end positions of the ball).
confidence.title: Prediction Confidence

end.description: the end of the ball's flight which happens when it bounces, hits the net, is hit by a paddle, or flies out of the video frame

location.description: Location of the ball when it ended its flight.
location.title: World XYZ

ms.description: Number of milliseconds into the video when the ball ended its flight.
ms.title: Video Milliseconds

zone.description: Zone where the ball ended its flight.
zone.title: Zone

peak.description: Location where the ball reached its highest (z) point.
peak.title: World XYZ

start.description: the moment the ball starts flying after being hit

location.description: Location where the ball was hit.
location.title: World XYZ

ms.description: Number of milliseconds into the video when the ball was hit.
ms.title: Video Milliseconds

zone.description: Court zone that the ball was hit from
zone.title: Zone

trajectory.title: Ball Flight Trajectory

resulting_ball_movement.title: Resulting Ball Movement

shot_type.description:
- smash: an overhead or similar shot where the ball goes from high to low (no upward motion)
- lob: a shot with a relatively high peak
- dink: a shot that would land in or near the kitchen and which was hit from near the kitchen
- drop: a shot that would land in or near the kitchen and was hit from the transition zone or deeper
- drive: a shot that would land deep if not stopped by an opponent's paddle, opponent's body, or the net (and doesn't fall into an earlier categorization)
- atp: an around-the-post shot, where the ball is hit outside the sideline and around the net post instead of over the net
- erne: a shot hit from outside the sideline by the kitchen (based on when the player's feet first touch after a volley)
- tweener: a shot where the ball is hit as it passes through the hitter's own legs

Omitted if we can't confidently determine a shot type based on the ball's trajectory and other characteristics.

start_ms.description: The time in milliseconds since the start of the video when the shot started.

stroke_side.description: The side of the body the stroke was made on. Omitted if unknown.

stroke_type.description: The type of stroke used to hit the ball. Omitted if unknown.

vertical_type.description: Whether the shot was hit as a dig, overhead, or neutral. Omitted if unknown.

winner_type.description: Whether the shot is a clean winner or forced an opponent fault. Omitted if this shot is not a winning shot.
